memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Harran. When he reached a certain place, he stopped for the night because the sun had set. Taking one of the stones there, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep." - Gen 28:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is Jacob at his lowest point. He has left home — fleeing his brother's murderous anger, cut off from his mother, alone in the open country. Night falls, and he has nothing but a stone for a pillow. No comforts, no company, no clear future. Just a fugitive lying down under the darkening sky.

Sometimes life brings us to a "stone pillow" place — a season stripped of comfort, where we feel alone and uncertain, perhaps facing the consequences of our own choices as Jacob was. It can be a lonely and frightening place to lie down at night.

But here is the wonder of this story: it is precisely in this comfortless place that God is about to meet Jacob in a way he will never forget. Jacob did not travel to a temple or a holy mountain. He simply lay down, exhausted and afraid — and God came to him there.

If you are in a stone-pillow season right now, take heart. God is not far from the lonely and the low. Some of His most tender encounters come to us not on the mountaintops of success, but in the wilderness of our weakness. The place where you feel most alone may be the very place God draws near.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I in a "stone pillow" season, stripped of comfort?
2. Do I believe God can meet me in my loneliest places?
3. How might my present wilderness be a place of divine encounter?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I lie down in lonely, comfortless places, remind me that You are near. Meet me in my wilderness as You met Jacob, and steady my fearful heart. Amen.
